title: Duchy of Greater Poland
capsule: The Duchy of Greater Poland emerged from the fragmentation of the Polish realm prescribed by Bolesław III Wrymouth's 1138 testament, which divided Poland into hereditary provincial duchies. Centred on Poznań and Gniezno — the original heartland of the Piast dynasty — it was the most prestigious of the successor duchies and repeatedly served as a base for reunification efforts. Władysław I the Elbow-high used it as a springboard to reunite most of the Polish duchies, being crowned King of Poland at Kraków in 1320; Greater Poland was thereafter absorbed into the reunified kingdom.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The duchy's general bounds are known from medieval chronicles and Piast genealogical records, but internal administrative boundaries fluctuated considerably as the duchy was repeatedly divided and reunited among competing Piast princes.
